HPA selector overlap check repeatedly serializes identical pod labels

### What happened?

`HPAsMatchingPods` calls `labels.Set.String()` for every pod before deduplicating label sets. Pods from the same ReplicaSet commonly have identical labels, so this repeatedly allocates and sorts the same data during HPA reconciliation.

This remains in [current master](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8f5bbad3e20a347aaae13afd78cc955e642c68e4/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/hpa_selector_store.go#L114-L122), after the selector-store change in #139142.

### What did you expect to happen?

Avoid repeated serialization when all pods have the same labels, while preserving matching for mixed label sets.

### How can we reproduce it?

Run the existing benchmark:

```sh
GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./pkg/controller/podautoscaler -run '^$' \
  -bench '^BenchmarkHPAsMatchingPodsParallel$/1000hpas_' -benchmem
```

With 1,000 HPA selectors, increasing identically labeled pods from 10 to 100 increases allocations from 31 to 301 per operation. The proposed fast path reduces both to 4.

### Environment

Local package benchmarks on Linux/amd64, Go 1.27.3. No cluster-level performance claim. Timings were collected at cb9115192fc; the affected code is unchanged at 8f5bbad3e20.

Expose per-resource storage write revision metric for watch cache and informer lag

[WatchCacheLag](https://perf-dash.k8s.io/#/?jobname=gce-5000Nodes&metriccategoryname=GenericMeasurements&metricname=WatchCacheLag) and InformerCacheLag compare `apiserver_watch_cache_resource_version` against the global `etcd_debugging_mvcc_current_revision`.

When a resource has no writes while other resources mutate, its watch cache RV stays at the last write until an etcd bookmark arrives. Because etcd bookmarks are infrequent, P99 lag is inflated idle phases (see graph below for services. The flat 0s at beginning and end are the only time services are changed, and sawtooth happens during times without writes.)

![Watch cache delay sawtooth during idle resource phases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jefftree/kubernetes/issue-assets/watch_cache_lag_services.png)

We should record the last written storage revision per resource (e.g. `apiserver_storage_resource_version{group, resource}`) on successful writes in [etcd3/store.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go) and compare `apiserver_watch_cache_resource_version` against that metric instead of the global etcd revision.

/sig api-machinery

textparse: OpenMetrics 2.0 puts classic histogram exemplars on `_count`, protobuf and OpenMetrics 1.0 put them on the matching `_bucket`

When the OpenMetrics 2.0 parser expands a classic histogram composite value into flat series, every exemplar on the line is returned with the first series, `_count` (or `_gcount`). `TestOpenMetrics2ParseExemplarOnCompositeLine` pins this.

The same histogram scraped as protobuf, or as OpenMetrics 1.0 (one exemplar per bucket line), stores each exemplar on the `_bucket` series whose bucket it falls in. The OpenMetrics 2.0 spec describes exemplars the same way ("An exemplar without Labels falls within the "0.1" bucket...", and recommends one exemplar per classic bucket).

So switching a target from OpenMetrics 1.0 or protobuf to OpenMetrics 2.0 moves its exemplars from `foo_bucket{le=...}` to `foo_count`. Exemplar queries that select the bucket series, such as those behind `histogram_quantile` panels, stop finding them.

Would you accept attaching each exemplar to the `_bucket` series with the smallest `le` >= the exemplar value (falling back to `+Inf`), as the other formats do? Happy to send the PR.

Related to #19745.

scrape: memory doubles for bodies over 59MB

### What did you do?

Scraped a target returning ~60MB of text, gzipped.

### What did you expect to see?

Memory proportional to one copy of the body.

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

Roughly double. The body sits on the heap twice for the whole parse.

Buffers come from a pool topping out at 59049000 bytes. Past that `Get` returns a slice sized exactly to the body, so `cap == len` and something has to reallocate:

- `ReadFrom` grows by `MinRead` before every `Read`, so the last one copies the buffer.
- `NewPromParser` appends a newline, same thing, and that copy lives as long as the parser.

Only `Content-Length` responses return the last bytes together with `io.EOF` and skip that final grow, so with gzip it is the read side that copies.

Reserving `MinRead` avoids both. One byte does not; the threshold is `MinRead`, not `cap > len`.

#19394 has the fix.

register_blueprint name override bypasses dot validation

The `Blueprint` constructor explicitly prevents dots in names (`if "." in name: raise ValueError`) because dots denote nested blueprints. However, `app.register_blueprint(..., name="...")` doesn't enforce this check on the overridden name.

If a blueprint is registered with a dot via the `name` kwarg, it bypasses the restriction. This tricks the framework into treating it as a nested blueprint, causing the parent's callbacks (like `before_request`) to unexpectedly execute for the unrelated child blueprint.

### How to replicate the bug
```python
import flask

app = flask.Flask(__name__)
parent = flask.Blueprint("parent", __name__)
child = flask.Blueprint("child", __name__)

parent.before_request(lambda: setattr(flask.g, "hit", True))
child.add_url_rule("/", "index", lambda: str(hasattr(flask.g, "hit")))

app.register_blueprint(parent)
app.register_blueprint(child, name="parent.fake") # Bypasses dot validation

print(app.test_client().get("/").get_data(as_text=True))

text:
Compose provider extensions/plugins can only execute ".exe" on windows

The Windows plugin discovery currently appears to restrict plugins to .exe files. I'm not sure this is desirable behavior.

https://github.com/docker/compose/blob/b3284911a304910035d1b9a5203f7b50190e1474/pkg/compose/plugins_windows.go#L22

On Windows, executable command resolution normally respects PATHEXT, which allows extensions such as .CMD, .BAT, and potentially .PY (depending on the environment) to be invoked without explicitly specifying the extension.

Restricting Compose plugins to .exe therefore prevents lightweight script-based plugins. For example, a plugin could be implemented as a Python, batch, or other script rather than requiring a compiled executable.

I think plugin discovery should probably respect PATHEXT (or otherwise use the same executable-resolution semantics as Windows), rather than hard-coding .exe.

This would also make Compose plugin behavior more consistent with how commands are normally resolved on Windows.

  const 한글Ref = useRef(0);
  return <div onClick={() => { 한글Ref.current += 1; }} />;
}
```

```
panicked at .../react_compiler_typeinference/src/infer_types.rs:
end byte index 1 is not a char boundary; it is inside '한' (bytes 0..3 of string)
```

Observed through oxlint 1.89.0, which vendors these crates. The line is unchanged on `main` (`compiler/crates/react_compiler_typeinference/src/infer_types.rs:249`). Any `*Ref` identifier whose first character is multi-byte (Korean, Japanese, emoji, ...) triggers it on `.current` access. The TS compiler is unaffected.

### Cause

```rust
&& object_name[..1]
    .chars()
    .next()
    .is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == '$' || c == '_')
```

`[..1]` slices a byte, not a character. The TS original (`/^(?:[a-zA-Z$_][a-zA-Z$_0-9]*)Ref$|^ref$/`) returns `false` for these names.

### Suggested fix

```rust
&& object_name
    .chars()
    .next()
    .is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == '$' || c == '_')
```

Same class of bug as #37539.

Bug: Fabric renderer should call dispatchNativeEvent when the event target is null

React Native PR https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/59522 (for https://github.com/react/react-native/issues/59519) lets `dispatchNativeEvent` accept a null target and still release the JS responder. This issue tracks the matching change in React.

React version: main (react-native-renderer, `ReactFabricEventEmitter.js`)

## Steps To Reproduce

1. In React Native, turn on `enableNativeEventTargetEventDispatching` and start a touch on a view.
2. Unmount that view before the touch ends, then tap any Pressable.

Link to code example: the React Native issue above has the details.

## The current behavior

The `eventTarget != null` guard in `ReactFabricEventEmitter.js` makes the renderer skip `dispatchNativeEvent` when the target is null. The touch end never reaches the JS responder. The old responder stays set, the touch count stays one too high, and the next tap is lost.

## The expected behavior

Remove the guard and let the Flow type for the target allow null. Then `dispatchNativeEvent` runs with a null target and releases the responder. React Native syncs this code from this repo, so the change must be made here. It must land after the React Native PR merges, because the current `dispatchNativeEvent` crashes on a null target.

Fragment observers retain removed child elements

## Description

Experimental Fragment refs apply registered `IntersectionObserver` and `ResizeObserver` instances to newly inserted element children, but the deletion path never calls `unobserve` for those observers. Once the child leaves the Fragment, `unobserveUsing` can no longer traverse to it, leaving the detached element observed and retained.

## Reproduction

Register an observer with a Fragment ref, dynamically render a second child, then remove that child. The observer receives `observe(child)` but never `unobserve(child)`.

## Expected behavior

Removing an element child should mirror insertion by unobserving it from every observer registered on the Fragment.

Fragment event listeners cannot be re-added after signal abort

## Description

Experimental Fragment refs retain listener registry entries registered with an `AbortSignal` after the signal removes those listeners from every host child. A subsequent add with the same type/callback/capture is treated as a duplicate and does nothing. An already-aborted signal is also recorded even though host elements reject the registration, blocking a later valid add.

## Reproduction

Register a Fragment listener with a signal, abort it, then register the same listener without that signal and click a host child. The second registration does not fire. The same occurs when the first registration receives a signal that was already aborted.

## Expected behavior

Aborted registrations should not prevent a later valid listener registration.

Turbopack: webpackChunkName ignored when migrating from webpack

### To Reproduce

1. Use a dynamic import with a `webpackChunkName` comment, such as React Player’s YouTube import below
2. Build with `next build --webpack` and observe the named chunk
3. Build with `next build` (Turbopack) and observe that the chunk name is lost

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Switching from webpack to Turbopack in Next.js 16.4.0 loses named dynamic-import chunks because Turbopack ignores existing `webpackChunkName` comments. For example, React Player names its YouTube import:

```js
import(
  /* webpackChunkName: 'reactPlayerYouTube' */
  'youtube-video-element/react'
)
```

webpack emits `reactPlayerYouTube.<hash>.js`, while Turbopack emits a generated filename such as `1z1qq2nqxoa77.js`.

Expected: preserve existing `webpackChunkName` names when switching from webpack to Turbopack, retaining a content hash in the filename.

### Use case

Identify third-party code in browser console messages and network requests. Our Playwright tests ignore a known YouTube progress log by its chunk URL. After switching to Turbopack, the filename no longer identifies the YouTube code, requiring a broader filter.

### Additional context

An implementation was proposed in #95409, but closed without merging.

Originally posted in https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/100010. Reporting here as a regression when migrating from webpack to the default Turbopack bundler.

v2.9.8 is tagged but has no release; v2.9.7 still trusts the distrusted eMudhra root

The 2026-10-17 eMudhra incident left eight Global TLS intermediate CA keys recoverable (they were integers 4, 56, 115, ...). Browsers blocked them via OneCRL/CRLSet and are distrusting `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`; `webpki-roots` 1.0.10 (2026-10-19) and Go 1.26.10/1.27.3 carry the removal.

**What we see in this repo:**
- Tag `v2.9.8` exists (`fe7ed012`), but there is **no GitHub release and no binaries** — the latest published release is still **v2.9.7 (2026-09-17)**, which predates the removal.
- The root store compiled into v2.9.7 still contains the eMudhra root, and Deno does not consult the OS store by default.

So anyone installing today gets a build that trusts the distrusted hierarchy, even though the fix is already on a tag.

**Ask:** publish v2.9.8 (or a 2.9.7 patch) with the updated root set, or say whether you are waiting on something upstream. If the root comes from `webpki-roots`, the bump is `1.0.10`.

No code issue claimed here — this is a release/remediation gap during a live incident. Happy to re-test and close if you consider it out of scope.

Disclosure: found with AI-assisted code review; the version facts above were checked against the GitHub releases API on 2026-10-21.

windows-aarch64 CI: libuv-sys-lite fails to build (bindgen produces opaque bindings on windows-11-arm runners)

The `test integration debug windows-aarch64` CI jobs fail while building the
`test_napi` helper crate:

```
Compiling libuv-sys-lite v1.48.3
error[E0425]: cannot find type `sockaddr_in` in this scope
error[E0080]: attempt to compute `1_usize - 128_usize`, which would overflow
  (many layout assertions: size_of::<uv_*_t>() == 1)

`libuv-sys-lite` ships pregenerated bindings for windows-x86_64 and
linux/macos (x86_64 + aarch64), but falls back to running bindgen at build

because `libuv-sys-lite` is restored from a warm cache; a cold rebuild of the
`deno` binary on those runners would hit the same error via `ext/napi`.

The proper fix is upstream: add pregenerated `bindings_windows_aarch64.rs` to
https://github.com/nathanwhit/libuv-sys-lite and release a new version (the
struct layouts should match windows-x86_64). Until then the napi integration
tests are skipped on windows-aarch64.

fix(ext/node): normalize process.resourceUsage maxRSS on macOS


Version: Deno build by latest code

## Problem

`process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` is approximately 1024 times larger than Node.js on macOS.

Deno currently returns `getrusage(2).ru_maxrss` directly:

```rust
r.ru_maxrss as f64
```

However, macOS and iOS report `ru_maxrss` in bytes, while Linux and most other Unix platforms report it in kilobytes.

libuv normalizes this value before exposing it through `uv_getrusage()`:

```cpp
#if defined(__APPLE__)
  rusage->ru_maxrss /= 1024;
#endif
```

As a result, a process with a peak RSS of approximately 100 MiB reports values similar to:

```text
Node.js: ~102400
Deno:    ~104857600
```

## Expected behavior

`process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` should use the same kilobyte unit as Node.js and libuv on macOS.

## Proposed fix

Normalize `ru_maxrss` by dividing it by 1024 on Apple platforms, while keeping the existing behavior on other Unix platforms.

Add a deterministic unit test for the conversion helper.

Remove redundant ServerAddressFromHostname call in registry Login

`pkg/registry/client.go` `(*Client).Login()` normalizes the credentials-store key twice:

```go
key := credentials.ServerAddressFromRegistry(host)
key = credentials.ServerAddressFromHostname(key)
```

The second line was added in 6ab7aa361 ("fix: legacy docker support broken for login") to work around oras-go v2.6.0, where `ServerAddressFromRegistry("registry-1.docker.io")` returned the host unchanged instead of the canonical `https://index.docker.io/v1/`.

That was fixed upstream in oras-project/oras-go#966, released in oras-go v2.6.1:

```go
func ServerAddressFromRegistry(registry string) string {
	if registry == "docker.io" || registry == "registry-1.docker.io" {
		return "https://index.docker.io/v1/"
	}
	return registry
}
```

Helm is already on oras-go v2.6.2, so `ServerAddressFromHostname` is now a no-op on the output of `ServerAddressFromRegistry` and the line can be deleted. Both Docker Hub host spellings should keep resolving to `https://index.docker.io/v1/`; the existing login tests cover this.

Scope: delete one line (plus the now-unneeded import, if nothing else in the file uses it). No `go.mod` change is needed.

Split out of #31386, which also covered the oras-go empty-credentials-file bug (oras-project/oras-go#959) — that one was fixed upstream before it needed a workaround in this tree, so this is all that is left.

Release branches cleanup policy

Helm creates release branches (of the format `release/v<Major>.<Minor>`) for each feature (minor) release.

Currently these accumulate, with no defined policy to clean them up. Helm does not support more than a single minor release version (per-major version), except in exceptional circumstances where a security patch has been backported to a prior release branch. Effectively meaning only the last one, or two in exceptional circumstances, release branches need to be retained.

To note, release branches can be recreated from a prior release tag (if needed).

Given the lack of patching of older release branches, a suggested policy is to clean up release branches >1 year old (policy suggested for simplicity, release branches don't need to live longer than ~6 months).

Issue for discussion and agreement.

Rule proposal: Require parentheses around multiline keyword argument expressions

I'd like to propose a rule that requires parentheses around multiline keyword argument values.

For example:

```python
return replace(
    self,
    account_id=account_id,
    period_defaulted=earlier.period_defaulted

Relative imports from a module named `__future__` are treated as future imports

### Summary

Ruff treats `from .__future__ import x` as a future import, even though the leading dot makes it an ordinary relative import of a sibling module named `__future__`. CPython accepts both statements below.

Eager import (any target version):

```python
from .__future__ import x
```

```console
$ printf 'from .__future__ import x\n' | ruff check --isolated --output-format concise --stdin-filename pkg/mod.py -
pkg/mod.py:1:25: F407 Future feature `x` is not defined
Found 1 error.
```

Lazy import (Python 3.15):

```python
lazy from .__future__ import x
```

```console
$ printf 'lazy from .__future__ import x\n' | ruff check --isolated --target-version py315 --select F407 --output-format concise --stdin-filename pkg/mod.py -
pkg/mod.py:1:1: invalid-syntax: lazy from __future__ import is not allowed
Found 1 error.
```

CPython 3.15.0 runs both statements:

```console
$ mkdir pkg && touch pkg/__init__.py
$ echo 'x = 1' > pkg/__future__.py
$ echo 'from .__future__ import x' > pkg/e.py
$ echo 'lazy from .__future__ import x' > pkg/d.py

ok
```

With the latest version of `uv` (built from Git sources with Rust v1.98.1), creation of a virtual env. with `uv venv` command:
```sh
openbsd-dev$ echo $KSH_VERSION
@(#)PD KSH v5.2.14 99/07/13.2
openbsd-dev$ uv -V
uv 0.13.0 (x86_64-unknown-openbsd)

openbsd-dev$ uv venv
Using CPython 3.14.8 interpreter at: /usr/local/bin/python
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Activate with: source .venv/bin/activate
```

There is an **error when trying to activate venv** with the described command:
```sh
openbsd-dev$ source .venv/bin/activate
ksh: source: not found
```

Indeed, on OpenBSD with ksh shell, **`source` command does not exist**. To activate virtual env, the correct command is `. .venv/bin/activate`.

To fix this issue (output of venv activate command with ksh), I propose to modify this function (new case for `Shell::Ksh`) in `crates/uv/src/commands/venv.rs`:

Warn/default-abort when installing conflicting packages

### What's the problem this feature will solve?

Naming collisions, while undesireable, do exist. `pip` could avoid making that problem worse -- currently it will happily try to install both packages on top of each other, creating an incoherent mess.

### Describe the solution you'd like

When asked to install two packages containing modules by the same name, `pip` should either warn or abort-by-default (perhaps leaving an escape hatch if someone knows what they're doing). Depending on the amount of metadata available to pip, this might only be possible when `pip` is already trying to unpack the wheel, but hopefully this can be done before any file is extracted.

### Alternative Solutions

- Strengthen PyPI policies against uploading colliding names -- likely expensive.
- Do nothing given this is relatively rare -- but the resulting bugs are hard to diagnose

### Additional context

One case where this comes up is when a PEP-541 request takes a while to process, so the original and new project exist simultaneously. In particular, this bit me with https://github.com/pypi/support/issues/9590

ENH: Simplify creating a ufunc at runtime (or produce a better error message)

### Proposed new feature or change:

Naive attempts of creating a new ufunc at runtime produce a misleading error message (at least with `numpy` 2.5.3 and Python 3.12.3):

New ufuncs can be created at runtime with [`np.frompyfunc()`](https://numpy.org/doc/2.5/reference/generated/numpy.frompyfunc.html). Revert broadcast_array deprecation expirery (gh-26214 )

See discussion starting with: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/32819#issuecomment-5927680798

The original PR had some unintended changes on top of the expiration. But additionally, there is a change that buffer-protocol export cannot give a `DeprecationWarning` so that some Cython users who ingest such arrays have to use `const`.

Those users _should_ prefer `const` and it is good that this get's fixed in SciPy, but we should also revert it anyway at least for a while (maybe 3.0).

One change that was _not_ intended is that this changed arrays to read-only that didn't need broadcasting. I think when reverting we should add a test for this so that if we expire the deprecation in the future we don't accidentally change that part again.[^1]

(There was an intermediate PR which added another new test to fix an initial issue. This test should be preserved as well.)

[^1]: It might not be completely strange to do this, but it's really not necessary and probably wasn't deprecated. Plus, I think if this was done then the code that relies on this would probably need a clearer API to achieve what it wants.

duplex(0) / zero-capacity in-memory pipe deadlocks on any write

**Version**
tokio master (latest)

**Platform**
Any (not platform-specific)

**Description**

Creating an in-memory pipe with a buffer size of 0 — `tokio::io::duplex(0)`, `simplex(0)`, or `SimplexStream::new_unsplit(0)` — deadlocks forever on the first non-empty write. The writer waits for free buffer space, the reader waits for data, but with a 0-byte buffer neither can ever happen.

I tried this code (it hangs forever):

```rust
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let (mut a, mut b) = tokio::io::duplex(0);
    tokio::join!(
        async { a.write_all(b"x").await.unwrap(); },
        async { let mut buf = [0u8; 1]; b.read(&mut buf).await.unwrap(); },
    );
}
```

I confirmed it hangs by wrapping it in a timeout, which always elapses.

Cause: in poll_write_internal (tokio/src/io/util/mem.rs), avail = max_buf_size - buffer.len() is always 0 when max_buf_size == 0, so every write registers a waker and returns Pending with no way to make progress.

Proposed fix: reject max_buf_size == 0 with a panic at construction, matching mpsc::channel(0) which already panics with "mpsc bounded channel requires buffer > 0". Happy to send a PR.

text:
Refactor: replace several vars with consts

### Overview
Several values are currently defined as package-level variables, even though they represent fixed configuration values that do not change at runtime.  
In Go, it is more idiomatic and safer to define such values as constants.

### Current Code
```go
var minCommandPathPadding = 11
var minNamePadding = 11
var defaultUsageTemplate = `Usage:{{if .Runnable}}...
var defaultHelpTemplate = `{{with (or .Long .Short)}}...
var defaultVersionTemplate = `{{with .DisplayName}}...
```

### Proposed Change
Update them to constants:
```go
const minCommandPathPadding = 11
const minNamePadding = 11
const defaultUsageTemplate = `Usage:{{if .Runnable}}...
const defaultHelpTemplate = `{{with (or .Long .Short)}}...
const defaultVersionTemplate = `{{with .DisplayName}}...
```

### Rationale
- These values are immutable and conceptually compile-time constants.
- Using const makes the intention clearer to readers and contributors.
- It prevents accidental modifications at runtime and improves overall code safety.

### Impact
This change is fully backward compatible and has no functional impact.
It simply improves the clarity and maintainability of the codebase.

chore(ui): centralize react-query cache updates in per-resource mutation hooks

# Summary

Add `ui/src/app/shared/mutations.ts` with per-resource `useMutation` hooks, next to the `queryOptions` factories in `shared/queries.ts`, so each mutation owns its cache update.

Follow-up to #30338, raised in review of #30544.

# Motivation

Pages migrated to react-query call `services.<resource>.<mutation>()` and then update the cache themselves with `invalidateQueries` or `setQueryData`. That pair is repeated at every call site, and more pages bring more copies. When a call site leaves out the cache update, or doesn't await it, the page keeps showing data from before the change.

# Proposal

- One hook per resource (`useProjectMutations(name)`, `useClusterMutations()`, `useGpgKeyMutations()`), wrapping `useMutation`, with the cache update in `onSuccess`.
- `onSuccess` returns the invalidation promise, so `mutateAsync` resolves after active queries have refetched.
- Error handling stays at the call site, keeping the existing per-action notifications.
- Use `isPending` instead of hand-rolled "updating" state.
- Move the pages already migrated (project details, clusters list/details, GnuPG keys) onto the hooks. Later migrations, starting with repositories and certificates, use them from the start.

COUNT shows `series.count` and LAST OCCURRED shows `series.lastObservedTime` when the legacy fields are not set. Backfilling them in the server conversion fixes the UI, CLI and API consumers at once.

otlpmetric, otlptrace: interpret compression environment enums case-insensitively

### Description

The log exporters interpret compression environment values case-insensitively (#9141, #9133); #9230 lands that by lowercasing the value in `convCompression` before matching.

The metric and trace exporters still compare exactly, so the shared variable behaves differently depending on the signal. With `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_COMPRESSION=GZIP`, the log exporters use gzip and the metric and trace exporters silently use no compression.

Four `WithEnvCompression` implementations parse the value with `if v == "gzip"`:

- `exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetricgrpc/internal/oconf/envconfig.go`
- `exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp/internal/oconf/envconfig.go`
- `exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc/internal/otlpconfig/envconfig.go`
- `exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp/internal/otlpconfig/envconfig.go`

The specification's environment enum guidance asks for case-insensitive interpretation, which is why #9141 and #9133 were filed for the log exporters.

This issue tracks bringing the metric and trace exporters in line with the log ones, so that a single shared variable resolves the same way for every signal. Work for the individual signals can reference this issue.

WithDefaultAttributes is overridden by nil attribute filter in views

Found while working on https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/8510

### Description

In the [OpenTelemetry Metrics SDK Specification](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/specification/metrics/sdk.md#view):

> "If attribute_keys is not provided, the SDK should use the 'Attributes' advisory parameter configured on the instrument. If that is also absent, all attributes are kept by default."

In the Go SDK's independent mode:

* When a user defines a view that modifies something unrelated to attributes (e.g., `NewView(Instrument{Name: "my_counter"}, Stream{Description: "updated"})`), NewView outputs `Stream{AttributeFilter: nil}`.
* Because a view matched, the pipeline skips the fallback block and uses `Stream{AttributeFilter: nil}` directly.
* As a result, the instrument's advisory Attributes (`metric/x.WithDefaultAttributes`) are completely dropped, and all recorded attributes are exported.

### Expected behavior

According to the specification, the stream should have retained the instrument's advisory attributes.

proposal: migrate pkg/internal/sets from set-gen to Go Generics

I would like to propose replacing the currently generated set implementation in pkg/internal/sets (specifically string.go and empty.go) with a single, modern Go generic implementation using type parameters (e.g., Set[T comparable] map[T]Empty).

If the project maintainers are open to this architectural update, I would be happy to submit a PR with the generic implementation alongside a comprehensive suite of unit tests.

Currently, the pkg/internal/sets package relies on code generated by set-gen (noted by the // Code generated by set-gen. DO NOT EDIT. header). This is a legacy approach from before Go 1.18 introduced generics.

Migrating this internal utility to native generics would provide several immediate benefits:

**1. Modernization:** It brings a core data structure up to modern Go standards.
**2. Maintainability:** It completely removes the package's reliance on external generator scripts and reduces code duplication.
**3. Testability:** It allows contributors to safely write and maintain standard unit tests for the data structure without the friction of modifying generated files.

Because kind already supports Go versions well past 1.18, this small refactor could safely clean up the internal utilities without impacting the rest of the codebase.
